projects.title: Design, Construction Supervision & Commissioning of a Sand Slurry Feed Regulating Sump (Jan 2014)
body: Provision of Project Management and Engineering services to design; provide construction supervision and commission a new feed regulating sump complete with rubber lined centrifugal slurry pump to pump sand/water slurry entering the sump from the client’s secondary vibrating screen to their recently commissioned sand plant. Incorporated into the design of the sump was an overflow weir and launder for wasting of the slimes; anti-turbulence baffles and clean outs. The project also entailed the decommissioning of the client’s Sand Classification system complete with product conveyors and electrical power & control systems.

projects.title: Geological Evaluation for proposed Sand & Gravel Quarry (Mar 2015)
body: EXPLORATION FOR SAND & GRAVEL – The project entailed the execution of a borehole drilling exercise to assess the reserve potential of a greenfield site. The site was inaccessible to heavy equipment and wheeled vehicles thus the need for man-portable drilling equipment. Boreholes were sunk to a depth of 15m and samples recovered for further testing and evaluation.

projects.title: Geo-technical Investigation
body: Conducted a Geotechnical Investigation for a three (3) storey residential building located at Valsayn, Trinidad. Works entailed field investigation, laboratory testing and engineering analysis.

projects.title: EIA & Certificate of Environmental Clearance CEC 4555/2015 (May 2016)
body: Conducted an Environmental Impact Assessment & Project Managed the acquisition of the necessary Statutory Environmental Clearances for CARMINCO’s proposed Sand & Gravel Quarry Project. To support the CEC Application for the project we formulated and prepared the project’s Environmental Management & Monitoring Plans; Rehabilitation Plans; Stormwater Management Plans & Mine Designs. Additionally, air, noise and water quality testing were conducted to establish environmental baselines for the project.

projects.title: Audit of Construction Materials Testing Laboratory’s Quality Management Systems & Practice (Sep 2016)
body: The Client commissioned our firm to conduct an audit of its lab’s Quality Management Systems and review of its Standard Operating Procedures and supporting documentation to identify improvements needed to improve the quality of their Lab’s outputs, training needs and deficiencies requiring attention to position its organisation as the premier supplier of ready-mix concrete to the local construction industry.

projects.title: EIA & Certificate of Environmental Clearance CEC 4601/2015 (Oct 2016)
body: Conducted an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) inclusive of baseline study for a proposed Sand & Gravel Quarry located at Tapana Valencia, Trinidad. Environmental Management & Monitoring Plans; Mine Design Plans; Rehabilitation Plans & Stormwater Management Plans were formulated for the project. On the basis of these plans the EMA granted a Certificate of Environmental Clearance (CEC) for the project.

projects.title: Aggregate Processing Plant Upgrade (Feb – Oct 2016)
body: Project Scope entailed Plant Foundation & Superstructure Design; Commissioning of new High Performance Aggregate Screening Machinery, Sand Processing Machinery; Redesign and upgrade of Aggregate Washing System; Infrastructure Design; Project Management; Construction Supervision and Plant commissioning.

projects.title: EIA & Certificate of Environmental Clearance 4331/2014 – Nov 2016
body: Conducted an Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and developed Environmental Management & Monitoring Plans; Mine Design Plans; Rehabilitation Plans & Stormwater Management Plans for Harry Persad & Son’s Ltd’s (HPSL) 36 Ha Sand & Gravel Quarry. Pursuant to the foregoing the Environmental Management Authority approved and granted CEC4331/2014 to HPSL.

projects.title: C&H Quarryworks Ltd. – Sand & Gravel Plant Refit and Upgrade (Dec 2013)
body: The Client owns what was once a derelict sand & gravel washing and screening plant. Terran Resources was retained to conduct an assessment of the plant to guide the clients investment strategy. On the basis of the assessment the client was able to access the financing to carry out a re-fit of the plant. Upon commencement of the re-fit Terran Resources was retained to provide the necessary project supervision.

projects.title: National Quarries Company Limited (NQCL) Quality Audit – Feb 2014
body: The Client retained the services of Terran Resources to conduct a review of its operations with the aim of resolving quality issues plaguing its aggregate products, in particular its concreting sand product. To this end an audit of its Laboratory and operations processes was commissioned. Upon completion of the audit our services were retained to conduct critical training of Laboratory Staff to support the resolution of the issues identified.

projects.title: Vega Minerals Wash Plant Upgrade
body: Upgrade to an aggregate wash plant including new foundation works and waste-water recycling facilities upgrade.

about.description: A specialist mineral resource management and construction materials consulting company registered in the United States of America with Operations in Florida and several Caribbean territories.

paragraphs: As human civilisation continues to flourish, further evolving into the 21st Century investment in infrastructure and physical development of our living space is an inescapable necessity. Our built environment cannot be advanced without materials extracted from our natural environment. Natural Resources such as mineral aggregates, limestone, gypsum, iron ore, silica, clay, bauxite and a host of other industrial minerals are important constituents of essential refined materials such as Cement, Steel, Aluminium, Concrete, metals, Asphalt and Glass. These, in addition to a host of other naturally occurring minerals comprise the essential building blocks of our Built Environment. Our daily lives are sustained through the consumption of a myriad of terran (latin derivative meaning "of or pertaining to the earth") resources. Whether it is mined or grown, modern civilisation cannot be sustained without the exploitation of the earth's resources. At the same time modern civilisation's trek into the new century cannot be allowed to continue to the detriment of the Biosphere's resilience.
